about.title: About
about.p1: Software developer and ESIGELEC engineering graduate, specialized in cybersecurity and networks, working mainly on backend and full-stack development.
about.p2: My experience covers web applications and REST APIs, language model integration through APIs, and cloud infrastructure with AWS, Docker and Linux. Most recently I spent four months in Taipei extending an open-source AI platform: working inside a large existing codebase, deciding what to change, and justifying those choices.
about.p3: I enjoy technical problems that require reading someone else's code carefully before writing my own.

reekon.role: R&D Software Developer — AI / Open WebUI
reekon.summary: Adaptation and extension of an AI assistant platform based on Open WebUI, inside a large open-source codebase receiving frequent upstream updates.
bullets: Extended the Python backend: new database tables, explicit assistant–model associations and persisted UI configuration, turning the platform into a real multi-assistant architecture.
Developed pipe functions connecting the platform to internal and external language models through APIs, with response streaming and output limiting to keep the interface responsive.
Made prompting dynamic: system prompts and behaviour adapt to the selected assistant and model.
Built Svelte interfaces with forms generated from JSON/YAML definitions, hiding technical structures from non-technical users.
Secured the AWS infrastructure (EC2, VPC, Security Groups) behind a self-hosted Headscale VPN after comparing WireGuard, Tailscale and Headscale, and optimized cloud resource usage.

atim.summary: Development of a tool estimating the battery life of IoT sensors from their configuration, later released as a public product page.
bullets: Implemented the energy consumption model: measurement count, logging, sending frequency, transmission, reception and sleep consumption, thresholds, temperature and battery capacity.
Modelled the supported sensor ranges (MR4, THx, THAQ, TMxP, TCR, LVL, PTMxP) and computed frame size and frame count, automating calculations previously done in Excel.
Extended the first web version with a Node.js API, then a C++/Qt desktop client communicating with it.
Resolved CORS, Linux compatibility and filesystem path issues introduced by the client/API split.
